subject: Blue Harbor - hybrid billing / Net-90 exception request
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@blueharbor.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@blueharbor.ai>
Date: Sat, 04 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing cadence question — Blue Harbor / Redwood

Markus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had an internal finance sync this morning and a couple of asks came up around how Redwood invoices for the proposed pilot. Blue Harbor's fiscal cadence is a bit unusual: we close budgets quarterly but our AP prefers to receive larger invoices on a quarterly basis and pay on Net-90 terms (we have a standard 90-day remit schedule tied to our quarter close).

Specifically: we'd like to request that the $150k annual subscription be invoiced quarterly (one invoice per quarter) with Net-90 payment terms, and any overage/consumption be invoiced monthly on Net-30. Our procurement team says they can sign the PO but need confirmation of the billing/currency and payment schedule to attach to the vendor record.

I'm attaching the PO and our procurement calendar for visibility. We understand longer terms create risk — we're open to prepaying a portion up front if that helps (the CFO suggested 15-25% prepay). Can you let me know what exceptions are possible and what approvals you'd need?

Appreciate it,
Jordan

Attachments: BlueHarbor_PO_2026-07.pdf (stub), BlueHarbor_Procurement_Calendar.xlsx (stub)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing cadence question — Blue Harbor / Redwood

Jordan — thanks for the clear note and the PO. We like Blue Harbor and want to keep the procurement path simple. Quick summary of what we can propose off the bat: 

- Quarterly subscription invoices for the base S1 plan (4 invoices/year) with Net-90 payment terms.
- Monthly invoices for usage/overage with Net-30 terms.
- To mitigate credit exposure on Net-90 for the quarterly invoice we require a 20% prepayment of the first quarter (applied as a credit to the first invoice) OR a 15% prepay + a 4% short-term financing fee applied to invoices paid on Net-90.

We need an executive exception for the Net-90 on the subscription line (policy is Net-30 standard). I have copied Vanessa (rev ops) and Jonas (deal desk) to confirm operational feasibility. If you can confirm which prepay option Blue Harbor prefers, we'll route this for exec sign-off and get a redlined SOW/Amendment and DocuSign link back to you within 48 hours.

Proposed next steps:
1) Jordan confirms prepay option (20% prepay OR 15% prepay + 4% fee).
2) We route to Deal Desk for approval + Sales Ops to create amended invoice schedule.
3) DocuSign sent and procurement executes.

Thanks — I loop in finance/ops internally to expedite.

Best,
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Blue Harbor - hybrid billing / Net-90 exception request — exec approval needed

Team — forwarding the request from Blue Harbor. Summary: enterprise pilot $150k ARR, asking to be invoiced quarterly with Net-90 on the subscription invoices. They offered prepay as a mitigant. My proposal (based on prior similar wins): require 20% prepay of first quarter (applied as credit), OR accept 15% prepay + 4% financing fee. Either option keeps exposure bounded.

Why this is strategic: Blue Harbor is a references-grade analytics customer in healthcare (potential ARR expansion toward $600k in 18 months). They have a procurement calendar that forces Net-90 for quarterly invoices — turned down vendors historically over this. We can win this if we accept a controlled exception.

Request: need an exec sign-off (legal/finance ok with optional fee) to allow Net-90 on subscription invoices conditioned on the prepay/fee. Please reply with one-line APPROVE / DENY and any conditions. If APPROVE, I'll ask RevOps to draft the amendment and Jonas to record the exception in Deal Desk.

Quoted for context:

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Blue Harbor - hybrid billing / Net-90 exception request — exec approval needed

All — after a quick review with Finance: APPROVE with the following conditions:

1) 20% prepayment of the first quarter applied as an upfront credit (preferred).
2) If Blue Harbor requests the 15% + 4% fee route, we require a Finance contact on the PO and the invoice must be flagged for collections escalation at Day 60.
3) Add the exception language to the SOW amendment, and include a 60-day review clause tied to early payment behavior before granting future Net-90 exceptions.

Jonas — please record the exception in Deal Desk (Deal ID DH-2026-1179) and create the DocuSign amendment. Priyom — coordinate the invoice schedule with RevOps and apply the appropriate invoice flags. Markus — please communicate the conditions back to Jordan and confirm which prepay option they choose.

Thanks — Laura
